attempts.summary: Built redundant dual-transit connectivity between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense), each fronting a private-network host (node3, node4 respectively). node1-node2 have two independent point-to-point transit links (10.10.1.0/30 via eth1/vtnet1 "Transit A", 10.10.2.0/30 via eth2/vtnet2 "Transit B"). node3 (10.10.3.0/24 on node1's eth3) and node4 (10.10.4.0/24 on node2's vtnet3) can reach each other across either transit path. On VyOS, an ECMP-style static route to 10.10.4.0/24 with two interface-bound next-hops automatically drops the down path from the FIB when a transit interface fails. On OPNsense, dpinger-monitored gateways (GW_TRANSIT_A/B) feed a gateway group used in a policy-route ("route-to") pf rule, with matching interface-bound reply-to and no-NAT exception rules to keep the traffic symmetric and bidirectional. Demonstrated live failover: started a continuous ping node3->node4, disabled node1's eth1 (Transit A), confirmed OPNsense's pf rule switched from route-to vtnet1 to route-to vtnet2, and verified zero packet loss / no sequence gaps in the ping log across the entire outage-and-failover window; then restored Transit A and confirmed the primary path resumed. Finally completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes, confirming changed boot identity (boot_id / kern.boottime) after each restart and full recovery of interfaces, routing, dpinger monitors, NAT/filter rules, and end-to-end node3<->node4 connectivity.
